prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Phoenix for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” dentist for implants in Phoenix — the right provider depends on your needs (single tooth vs full-arch, bone-grafting or sinus lift required, medical history, budget, desire for sedation, etc.). That said, the dentists you should consider are usually specialists who place implants frequently: oral & maxillofacial surgeons, periodontists, and prosthodontists. Here’s a quick plan to find the best match for you plus what to ask at a consult.

What type of specialist to look for
- Oral & maxillofacial surgeon: best for complex surgeries, extractions, bone grafts, sinus lifts, medical-complex patients, or IV sedation.
- Periodontist: specializes in the gums and bone and commonly places implants; great for bone grafting and esthetic cases.
- Prosthodontist: specializes in the restoration (crowns, bridges, full-arch prostheses) and often manages the final implant tooth for complex restorative cases.
- General dentists with advanced implant training can be excellent for straightforward single-implant cases — check experience and referrals.

How to find high-quality implant providers in Phoenix
- Search Google/Yelp/Healthgrades/Zocdoc and sort by reviews, but treat reviews as one data point.
- Check professional credentials: DDS/DMD plus fellowship or board certification (American Board of Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery, American Board of Periodontology, American College of Prosthodontists, AAID Fellowship).
- Look for modern technology: cone-beam CT (CBCT), digital planning and guided surgery, in-house lab/strong lab partnerships.
- Ask how many implants the doctor places per year and to see before/after photos of cases like yours.
- Verify they work with a restorative dentist (if the surgeon places implants, you want coordinated care for the crown/prosthesis).

Key questions to ask at the consultation
- Are you a specialist? What are your credentials and implant training?
- How many implant cases do you place per year? How many similar to mine?
- Do you use CBCT and guided surgery?
- What implant systems do you use and why?
- Will you handle both the surgical and restorative phases or coordinate with my dentist?
- What are the risks, success rate, and expected timeline?
- Do I need bone grafting or sinus lift? If so, how long until implant placement?
- Can I see before/after photos and patient references?
- What is the total cost (surgery + implant + abutment + crown/prosthesis) and payment/insurance options?
- What is your follow-up/emergency policy and warranty for implant work?

Red flags to avoid
- No CBCT for treatment planning when bone anatomy is uncertain.
- Very low prices with no clear explanation of materials/brand.
- Surgeon who won’t share photos, references, or case numbers.
- Staff is evasive about costs, or the clinician rushes consults.

If you want, I can:
- Narrow recommendations if you share your Phoenix ZIP code and whether you need a simple single implant or a complex/full-arch solution.
- Provide a checklist you can print and bring to consults.

Which would you prefer — a shortlist of local providers (please give ZIP) or a printable checklist of questions to bring to appointments?
